stem.text: Consider the differential equation \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} = (x + 1)(4 - y) \). Let \( y = f(x) \) be the particular solution to the differential equation with the initial condition \( f(0) = 2 \). It is known that \( f(x) < 4 \) for all real \( x \).

parts.prompt: Find \( \dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} \) in terms of \( x \) and \( y \). Then find the value of \( f''(0) \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the right side with the product rule, treating y as a function of x.
Substitute the differential equation for dy/dx.

points.criterion: Gives d^2y/dx^2 in terms of x and y only: (4 - y) - (x + 1)^2(4 - y), or any equivalent form such as (4 - y)(1 - (x + 1)^2) or -x(x + 2)(4 - y). An expression still containing dy/dx does not earn the point.
Evaluates the second derivative at x = 0, y = 2 and gives f''(0) = 0.

parts.prompt: The line tangent to the graph of \( f \) at \( x = 0 \) is \( y = 2 + 2x \). It gives the approximations \( f(0.3) \approx 2.6 \) and \( f(-0.3) \approx 1.4 \). For each approximation, determine whether it is an overestimate or an underestimate of the value of \( f \). Give a reason for each answer.
parts.answer_latex: f(0.3) \approx 2.6 \text{ is an overestimate}; \quad f(-0.3) \approx 1.4 \text{ is an underestimate}

worked_solution.text: For 0 < x <= 0.3, (x + 1)^2 > 1 and 4 - y > 0, so the second derivative is negative and f is concave down there.
A concave down graph lies below its tangent line, so 2.6 is an overestimate.
For -0.3 <= x < 0, 0 < (x + 1)^2 < 1 and 4 - y > 0, so the second derivative is positive and f is concave up there.
A concave up graph lies above its tangent line, so 1.4 is an underestimate.

points.criterion: States that f(0.3) is overestimated, because d^2y/dx^2 < 0 for all x with 0 < x <= 0.3 (since 4 - y > 0 and 1 - (x + 1)^2 < 0), so the graph of f is concave down on that interval and lies below the tangent line. Citing only f''(0) = 0, or the sign at a single point, does not earn the point.

States that f(-0.3) is underestimated, because d^2y/dx^2 > 0 for all x with -0.3 <= x < 0 (since 4 - y > 0 and 1 - (x + 1)^2 > 0), so the graph of f is concave up on that interval and lies above the tangent line. Citing the sign at a single point does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Let \( y = g(x) \) be the particular solution to the same differential equation with \( g\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) = 8 \), where \( g(x) > 4 \) for all \( x \), and let \( y = h(x) \) be the particular solution with \( h\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) = 2 \), where \( h(x) < 4 \) for all \( x \). Find \( g''\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) \) and \( h''\left(-\tfrac{1}{2}\right) \). The lines tangent to the graphs of \( g \) and \( h \) at \( x = -\tfrac{1}{2} \) give the approximations \( g(-0.3) \approx 7.6 \) and \( h(-0.2) \approx 2.3 \). For each approximation, determine whether it is an overestimate or an underestimate. Give a reason for each answer.
parts.answer_latex: g(-0.3) \approx 7.6 \text{ is an overestimate}; \quad h(-0.2) \approx 2.3 \text{ is an underestimate}

worked_solution.text: For -1/2 <= x <= -0.2, 0 < x + 1 < 1, so 1 - (x + 1)^2 > 0. Since 4 - g < 0, g is concave down on [-1/2, -0.3] and its graph lies below the tangent line.
Since 4 - h > 0, h is concave up on [-1/2, -0.2] and its graph lies above the tangent line.

points.criterion: Evaluates the second derivative at x = -1/2, y = 8 and gives g''(-1/2) = -3.

States that g(-0.3) is overestimated, because d^2y/dx^2 < 0 for all x in -1/2 <= x <= -0.3 on the graph of g (4 - g < 0 and 1 - (x + 1)^2 > 0 there), so g is concave down and lies below its tangent line. Citing only g''(-1/2) < 0 does not earn the point.
Evaluates the second derivative at x = -1/2, y = 2 and gives h''(-1/2) = 3/2, or 1.5.

States that h(-0.2) is underestimated, because d^2y/dx^2 > 0 for all x in -1/2 <= x <= -0.2 on the graph of h (4 - h > 0 and 1 - (x + 1)^2 > 0 there), so h is concave up and lies above its tangent line. Citing only h''(-1/2) > 0 does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Euler's method, starting at \( x = 0 \) with two steps of size \( 0.2 \), gives the approximation \( f(0.4) \approx 2.784 \). Is this approximation an overestimate or an underestimate of \( f(0.4) \)? Give a reason for your answer.

worked_solution.text: For 0 < x <= 0.4 and y < 4, 1 - (x + 1)^2 < 0 and 4 - y > 0, so every solution curve in that region is concave down, and the Euler points stay in that region.
Each Euler step follows a tangent segment that lies above a concave down solution curve, so the approximation is too large.

points.criterion: States that 2.784 is an overestimate, because d^2y/dx^2 < 0 for 0 < x <= 0.4 wherever y < 4, so the solution curves there are concave down and the Euler tangent segments lie above them. An argument from the sign at x = 0 alone, or from f increasing, does not earn the point.
